source_text: Ταύτῃ τειχίζεται, βασιλεῦ, τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας σου κράτος· ταύτην ἡμῖν ἄσυλον διαφύλαττε. Μηδεὶς αἱρετικὸς, ὑποδὺς τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν, ἕν τι τῆς Τριάδος ἀφαιρείτω, καταλιμπάνων τὸ λειπόμενον ἄτιμον.
thought_title: Guard the Faith as a Wall
orientation: Eustathius is addressing Emperor Constantine directly, urging him to protect the orthodox faith of the Trinity from heretics.
pass_a_gloss: By this [faith] is walled, emperor, the power of your true faith; this [faith] for us [as] inviolable keep. Let no heretic, slipping under the Church, one [person] of the Trinity take away, leaving the remainder dishonored.

choices.why: Literal passive of τειχίζω, preserving the metaphor of the faith as a defensive wall
Literal aorist participle of ὑποδύω, conveying stealthy entry into the Church
Third-person imperative, preserving the command force directed at any heretic
Literal adjective, emphasizing the loss of honor to the remaining persons of the Trinity

pass_b_english: By this, emperor, the power of your true faith is walled about; keep it inviolable for us. Let no heretic slip under the Church and take away one of the Trinity, leaving what remains dishonored.
